$comment: T12, spec 2026-08-29-parity-judgement-gates-and-evals. THE LEDGER of every point in the Figma<->code pipeline where an agent makes a judgement rather than a computation. The 13 below were found by a one-off read-only sweep on 2026-08-29; nothing would have surfaced the 14th, which is what this file plus scripts/check-judgement-ledger.mjs exist to fix. `disposition` is what NOW checks each one: `gated` = a deterministic check refuses the bad answer, `evaluated` = an eval measures how often the agent gets it right, `open` = still nothing. An `open` entry is not a bug in this file; it is the honest state, and the file exists so it stays visible.

dispositions.gated: a deterministic check now refuses the wrong answer outright
dispositions.evaluated: an eval measures it; the wrong answer is possible but scored

points.decision: Adopt the Figma change into code, or revert Figma to the code truth?
points.anchor: First decide direction with a human
points.wrongAnswer: Figma silently becomes the source of truth for a token value, reversing the DTCG generation direction CLAUDE.md calls one-way.

points.decision: On `conflict`, which side wins per property?
coveredBy: task E — the `both-sides-changed` case, whose answer is ask-a-human
points.wrongAnswer: A half-merge; one side's intent is silently lost with no record that it existed.

points.decision: Should a Figma-only set exist in code at all?
points.anchor: Decide with a human whether it should exist in code
points.wrongAnswer: Scaffolding a layout wrapper the repo's arrangement guardrails ban, to turn a badge green.

points.decision: Repair the set in place, or regenerate it?
points.anchor: never delete+rebuild a pinned atom set
points.wrongAnswer: New node ids are minted; every pinned reference and prop-sheet entry is orphaned.

points.decision: Is it actually reconciled — may I stamp `in-sync`?
coveredBy: T1: check-parity.mjs exits non-zero and writes a receipt; mark-synced refuses without a fresh passing one
points.wrongAnswer: A green `in-sync` badge over a broken set — the state every parity surface reports.

points.decision: Is this reconciliation plan any good?
coveredBy: task D (reconciliation accuracy) — precision/recall against contract-diff.mjs
points.wrongAnswer: A confident plan written against a Figma observation that was never refreshed.

coveredBy: task F (curation review) — derived live from the 33 tracked curation files
points.wrongAnswer: al-badge sampled as a dot; al-banner sized by whatever message text happened to be there.

points.decision: Fan a prop out as an `axis`, `omit` it, or curate `pairWith`?
coveredBy: task F — including the al-button T22/T23 -> T31 reversal as a hand-authored negative case
points.wrongAnswer: The real one: a ~200-variant fan-out curated from a documentation screenshot mistaken for the live set.

points.decision: Is this verify miss a generic-rule gap, a missing measured fact, a curation call, or a site bug?
points.wrongAnswer: A per-component hack lands in shared generator code — the one thing the generate skill forbids outright.
points.note: Not evaluated yet. The classification only exists inside a live generation session, so a case would have to be captured from a real verify report rather than derived.

points.decision: Has it converged — is a remaining row an accepted degradation?
points.anchor: the numeric verify + auto-exported image pair are the critic
points.wrongAnswer: Stopping early and declaring residual drift acceptable, with no record of what was accepted.

points.decision: Does the render actually look right — colour, glyph, label text?
coveredBy: T4: verify-figma.mjs now compares text, fill colour and fill-boundness (scripts/lib/visual-facts.mjs)
points.wrongAnswer: The snippet skill's trap 9: the chips 'looked right' red at thumbnail scale and the eyeball was wrong.
points.note: The comparator half is gated but REPORT-ONLY until someone runs it live and reads the false-positive rate (`--gate-facts`). Whatever the comparator cannot express is still open — see spec task T10.

points.decision: Is this `missingVars` entry expected noise or a real loss?
points.wrongAnswer: Real arrangement loss dismissed as 'expected', silently.

points.decision: Applying the library's Figma conventions by hand — page name, axis order, Title Case values.
points.anchor: State axis, Title Case variant values
coveredBy: T3: scripts/check-figma-conventions.mjs (Title Case, State vocabulary, set name)
points.wrongAnswer: A non-conforming set that still passes every other gate.
points.note: Variant ORDER remains unverifiable from a canvas contract: extract-canvas.mjs sorts axis options, so the artifact records the set and destroys the order.

points.decision: Is the Figma document I am measuring the project's file at all?
coveredBy: assertTargetFile() refuses unless the ACTIVE file key equals project.figma.fileKey
check-parity.mjs runs it before taking a single measurement
the receipt records observedFileKey, and receiptAuthorises() refuses a receipt from another file or one that does not say
points.wrongAnswer: A receipt minted against whatever file happened to be active becomes proof of parity with the target. Found live on 2026-08-29: a client file ("Hooper Design System") was the ACTIVE document while this tooling was pointed at Altitude. checkDecoyGuard passed it because it is not on the known-bad list, and nothing downstream recorded which file the measurement came from - the receipt stored project.figma.fileName, what it INTENDED to measure, never what it did. This is the 14th point; the ledger existed to make it visible, and the guard it demanded is allowlist-shaped, per this repo's own rule that a negative guard let a client file through once already.

$acknowledgedComment: Files that CARRY a judgment-call marker in a comment but are not themselves a ledger point: they are either generation-internal curation already covered by J7 (the figma/ modules, all reached through component-config.mjs), or unrelated to the Figma<->code lane (check-token-usage.mjs). Listing them is deliberate — it is what lets the checker fail on a marker in a file NOBODY has looked at, instead of on every marker in the repo.
